text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Pakistan announces a mini-budget, devalues the rupee by 8.5 percent, raises REPO rate to 20 percent from 17, increases petroleum prices by 10 percent and raises excise duty on gas distribution by 10 percent.

- Central bank governor presented a package providing for a heavy tax-loaded second budget to raise additional revenue of 13 billion rupees and generate savings of 27 billion -- 20 billion by cutting down on development programme and seven billion by applying economy cuts on current expenditure.
- Sindh provincial government levies five percent tax on services.

- President Farooq Leghari has promulgated an ordinance giving immediate effect to a number of important changes introduced by the government in the central excise, customs, income tax and sales tax laws.
- One person was gunned down and four others were injured in a mosque near Multan in central Pakistan.
- The International Monetary Fund team will reach Pakistan on Friday.
- Leghari presided over a high-level meeting to discuss the security situation in the region with special reference to its implications on Pakistan and Afghanistan.
- Bank of America has entered agreements with two nationalised banks to finance wheat imports of up to $125 million. The financing will be available for three years.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Central bank governor said the devaluation of the rupee had been done for the stabilisation of the economy.
- Marginal bank lending rates are expected to range between 25 and 28 percent with the interbank call rate at 22 percent.
- Gold prices shot up 350 rupees to 5,900 per tola in Lahore after the rupee's devaluation.
FINANCIAL POST

- The central bank decided that the rupee equivalent of any incremental foreign currency deposit accepted by authorised dealers between October 21 and November 28 under existing rules can be deposited with the central bank in a special account earning interest at 17 percent a year.
- Pakistan's debt payment was estimated at $2 billion by the end of June 1997 of which $700 million is due by November.
THE NATION

- Opposition Pakistan Muslim League leader Nawaz Sharif said the latest rupee devaluation would prove to be the straw that broke the camel's back as neither the economy nor the common man could bear this additional burden.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's economic adviser V.A. Jafarey offered his resignation last week, but it was not immediately accepted.
THE NEWS

- Pakistan's Foreign Office said a U.N. Security Council resolution on Afghanistan "betrays a certain lack of resolve to take urgent and effective measures to end the massive foreign interference including supply of weapons and equipment to some of the Afghan parties".
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and President Farooq Leghari were briefed by Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar on his peace mission to Afghanistan.
